result:
Solution 2 gives the correct final answer, N(N+1)/2. I recalled this from the literature on rational solutions of the massive Thirring model, which I believe states that under the real-root assumption the N-th rational solution has N(N+1)/2 poles in the upper half x-plane for large |t|. I did not verify this against the paper, so my confidence is moderate.

The result is consistent with N = 1: a single algebraic soliton gives one pole in each half-plane, so one pole in the upper half-plane. Solutions 1 and 3 both give N, which matches N = 1 but fails for N ≥ 2. Solution 2's justification (degree N(N+1) denominator with all zeros in conjugate pairs) is not fully convincing, but its final answer is the one I believe is correct.

CHOICE: 2
